company: Gujarat Narmada Valley Fertilizers & Chemicals Ltd
units: INR crore unless stated. Consolidated = standalone + 46.87% associate GGRC (equity method, ~Rs11-12 cr a year). Screener's consolidated figures match the company's.

profile.incorporated: 1976 (Bharuch, Gujarat); operations from 1982 with one of the world's largest single-stream ammonia-urea complexes (q4fy26Deck p41)
profile.promoters: Gujarat State Investments Ltd 21.44% + Gujarat State Fertilizers & Chemicals Ltd 19.86% = 41.30%, unchanged (AR FY26 note 17.3-17.5; Jun-2026 BSE pattern)
profile.sharesNote: 14,69,40,683 shares of Rs10 after the Dec-2023 buyback; no change since (AR FY26 note 17)

fy26Production.src: AR FY26 MD&A capacity table (rated vs produced)

profile.uniqueness: Only TDI maker in South-East Asia and the Indian subcontinent; India's only glacial acetic acid by methanol carbonylation; only oil-based ammonia in India; largest formic acid maker (q4fy26Deck p8)
profile.tdiMarket: Indian TDI use ~1 lakh t in flexible foam + 10-15 kt in system houses; GNFC share ~60%, rest imported; market growing ~10% a year; FY25 TDI sales 50,500 t (TDI-II shut four months); TDI capacity utilisation ~80%, near the global norm (q3fy26Call; q4fy26Call)
profile.aniline: Not viable on a stand-alone basis against Chinese aniline (coal-based hydrogen, 7-8x single-site scale); GNFC does job work for other companies on a fixed margin; ADD Wanhua $37/t, others $121/t; aniline ADD extended to mid-2030 (q4fy26Call; q1fy26Call)
profile.tgu: Technical-grade urea (for diesel exhaust fluid, plywood, cattle feed): rated 169 kt; >210 kt in FY26 as GNFC doubled TGU output in Mar-2026 when the war cut DEF supply; must first meet 637 kt of neem-coated urea for DoF (q4fy26Call; q1fy27Call)

fy26.oneTimers: ~Rs80 cr in FY26 (Rs30 cr in Q4) vs ~Rs38 cr in FY25: insurance ~Rs28 cr, urea freight escalation ~Rs15 cr, catalyst dust sale, CCPP-delay penalty from the contractor (q4fy26Call)
fy26.subsidyNote: AR FY26 notes 11, 27.2; subsidy outstanding Rs302 cr at Dec-2025 (q3fy26Call)

treasuryMar26.cashNote: cash & equivalents 74.18 + other bank balances 1,035.01 (deposits 935.72, unpaid dividend 28.72, escrow 48.15, CSR 22.42)
treasuryMar26.note: ICDs are 'deposits with a body corporate' (Gujarat State Financial Services) at ~7.25% (q4fy26Call); Screener shows them in 'Loans n Advances'. CFO: ~Rs4,000 cr of cash 'across G-Sec, GSFS and bank' (q1fy27Call). GSPC/GSPL shares swapped into Gujarat Gas shares under the 2026 merger scheme.

q1fy27.prices: TDI Rs255k/t (Q4 Rs220k), toluene Rs88k; aniline Rs169k, benzene Rs97k; acetic acid Rs63k, methanol Rs51k; fuel oil Rs73k/t (+76% QoQ), non-urea gas Rs73k/'000 SM3 (+64%), imported coal Rs12k/t (+6%)
q1fy27.production: ammonia ~173 kt (54% oil route); TDI 12,800 t (66% Dahej); WNA 113 kt; CNA 37.5 kt; AN melt 55.6 kt; TGU 74.8 kt; formic acid 8.2 kt

q1fy27Call: Second-highest quarterly profit in GNFC's history after Q1FY22; 'this typically happens in a war-like situation, it can go either side'.

Acetic acid (shut 6-May to 1-Aug), ethyl acetate (Q1 and July) and part of TDI (Bharuch TDI down in July) were not run for cost/viability reasons; offtake weaker than production, so inventory built up; ~15% liquidated by end-July at 'mixed' realisations.

Urea energy norm raised from 6.20 to 6.37 Gcal/t for 1-Apr-2025 to 31-Mar-2028 (DoF notification 30-Jun-2026): ~Rs61 cr gain for Apr-25 to Jun-26 to be booked in Q2FY27. Fixed-cost revision still pursued at industry level.
Fertiliser loss widened from Rs24 cr to Rs85 cr QoQ (urea ~Rs48 cr, ANP ~Rs12 cr of the change) on higher input costs, the Q4 one-timer and fixed costs.
Dahej coal-based steam & power plant (CCPP, Rs613 cr): steam running, power in ~45 days; saves ~Rs30,000-40,000 per tonne of TDI-II at current gas and coal prices.
WNA-III ~3 months late (recoupable); ammonia loop upgrade (AMUGL) and AN melt-II on track; all commercially operational around mid-2027.

Capex: Rs300 cr in Q1; FY27 another Rs1,200-1,500 cr (Rs1,500-1,800 cr in all); projects on hand Rs2,800 cr, of which ~Rs1,500 cr to be spent over the next two years; new projects (BPA, polyols, acetic acid) separate.
Projects to add Rs1,200-1,500 cr of revenue and Rs500-600 cr of contribution ('range for the current part of prognosis is difficult').
Kearney cost programme: initially Rs250-300 cr of savings; quantification not yet signed off.
Cash ~Rs4,000 cr across G-Secs, GSFS deposits and banks.
MoU proposed with GMDC for underground coal gasification (studies ongoing).
No guidance policy: 'we do not comment or give guidance on future results' (deck p2).
q4fy26Call: War from late Feb/early Mar 2026 hit TDI and neem-urea volumes; TGU doubled in March to cover a national DEF shortage; ammonium nitrate supplied to a short market.
FY26 PAT Rs797 cr (+35%); chemical prices up 6-28% QoQ in Q4 (all products except formic acid); TDI, AN and TGU drove the Rs300 cr QoQ EBITDA jump.
Fertiliser losses widening until energy norms and fixed costs are revised: 'almost no chance in case of urea' to turn profitable before that.
ICDs ~Rs2,400 cr with Gujarat State Financial Services at ~7.25%, a temporary yield decision 'till the time our capex cycle is over'.
No buyback in the pipeline. New urea investment policy: would evaluate against unregulated chemical opportunities.
Planned shutdown in April 2027. FY27 capex ~Rs2,800 cr (later cut to Rs1,500-1,800 cr in Aug). INEOS: licensing route instead of the earlier JV idea.
Pricing: variable-price contracts of one to three months, linked to import parity; TDI price includes anti-dumping duty in import parity.
earlierCalls: Feb-2026: TDI anti-dumping duty extended five more years; TDI share ~60% of India; Kearney savings Rs260-300 cr identified, Rs5-7 cr realised so far; projects Rs2,800 cr (WNA-III Rs1,420 cr, AN melt Rs357-450 cr, AMUGL Rs330 cr, CCPP Rs613 cr), ~Rs1,000 cr spent by Dec-2025; new Bharuch boiler Rs480-500 cr approved; CCPP net contribution ~Rs82 cr a year (q3fy26Call).
Nov-2025: BPA/phenol/polyols feasibility by Kearney; capex of both 'roughly Rs7,000-8,000 cr' including an upstream phenol plant (q2fy26Call).
Aug-2025: TDI-II does not recover its fixed costs at recent prices; Bharuch turnaround cost ~Rs375 cr of revenue and ~Rs148 cr of PBT in Q1FY26; aniline ADD extended to mid-2030 (q1fy26Call).
May-2025: maintenance capex ~Rs200 cr a year; Kearney expansion 'kitty' of Rs15,000-22,000 cr discussed (q4fy25Call).
projects: Steam running by Aug-2026, power expected ~45 days later; cuts TDI-II gas cost
Under consideration: BPA 150 KTPA, polyols 100 KTPA (Dahej), acetic acid 350 KTPA (Bharuch)
Decision expected by end-2026; INEOS licensing for acetic acid
history: Incorporated as a joint-sector company promoted by the Government of Gujarat and GSFC; Bharuch ammonia-urea complex starts in 1982
Diversifies into chemicals: methanol, formic acid, nitric acids, ANP (1991), acetic acid and aniline (1995), TDI-I (1998)
Methanol synthesis unit, CNA-III, WNA-II, ethyl acetate, gas-based ammonia syngas plant (2013) and the 50 KTPA TDI-II plant at Dahej (2014)
FY15
The only loss year in 50 years (net loss Rs443 cr) as TDI-II started and debt peaked (Rs3,844 cr)
Debt repaid from TDI and chemical profits; net cash by FY21
Post-COVID chemical boom: record PAT Rs1,710 cr (FY22) and Rs1,472 cr (FY23)
Buyback of 84,78,100 shares (5.46%) at Rs770 for Rs652.81 cr; shares now 14.69 cr
Chinese oversupply: chemical EBIT falls to Rs543 cr (FY24); TDI-II shut four months in FY25; Kearney hired as cost and strategy consultant (in place by May-2025)
Anti-dumping duty on TDI from the EU and Saudi Arabia extended for five years
US-Iran war: chemical prices spike; GNFC doubles TGU output for DEF; stock low ~Rs365 (30-Mar-2026)
Jun-Aug 2026
Urea energy norm raised to 6.37 Gcal/t (30-Jun); Q1FY27 PAT Rs312 cr; CCPP steam starts; GMDC coal-gasification MoU proposed
Sanjeev Kumar, IAS appointed MD (9-Sep), the fourth MD since Feb-2025; Rs21 dividend approved at the 50th AGM (16-Sep)
